title: Grieneisen, Xu, Marée, Hogeweg & Scheres (2007) Nature & Mähönen et al. (2014) Nature — Reverse-Fountain Root Tip Auxin Reflux Capacitor, Quiescent Center Exponential Accumulation, and PLETHORA Meristem Zonality in Arabidopsis thaliana
organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (primary root apex: vascular stele, pericycle/endodermis, cortex, epidermis/lateral root cap, quiescent center, and columella)

primary_sources.citation: Grieneisen, Xu, Marée, Hogeweg & Scheres (2007) Nature 449(7165):1008-1013
primary_sources.role: Establishes the 2D multi-file root tip reverse-fountain auxin reflux loop model (downward/rootward PIN1/PIN3/PIN7 transport in vascular stele at velocity +v_s, isotropic/lateral PIN3/PIN4/PIN7 redistribution in the Quiescent Center and columella, upward/shootward PIN2 transport in lateral root cap and epidermis at velocity -v_e, and inward lateral PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 reflux rate k_lat across cortex/endodermis back into the vascular stele), generating an exponential reflux capacitor with >100-fold QC auxin maximum that persists autonomously after shoot decapitation (J_in = 0) and rapidly regenerates a shifted QC peak upon laser ablation

primary_sources.citation: Mähönen, ten Tusscher, Siligato, Smetana, Díaz-Triviño, Salojärvi, Wachsman, Prasad, Heidstra & Scheres (2014) Nature 515(7525):125-129
primary_sources.role: Demonstrates how the root tip auxin maximum induces slow, stable PLETHORA (PLT1/PLT2) transcription factor synthesis that spreads via cell-to-cell movement and growth dilution to form a smooth axial PLT dosage gradient defining Stem Cell Niche / Quiescent Center (high PLT), Meristematic Zone (intermediate PLT > Theta_MZ), Elongation Zone (Theta_EZ < PLT <= Theta_MZ), and Differentiation Zone (PLT <= Theta_EZ)

primary_sources.citation: Blilou, Xu, Wildwater, Willemsen, Paponov, Friml, Heidstra, Aida, Palme & Scheres (2005) Nature 433(7021):39-44
primary_sources.role: Experimental characterization of synergistic PIN1, PIN2, PIN3, PIN4, and PIN7 polar localization domains and root meristem size defects in single and multiple pin mutants

primary_sources.citation: Sabatini, Beis, Wolkenfelt, Murfett, Guilfoyle, Malamy, Benfey, Leyser, Bechtold, Weisbeek & Scheres (1999) Cell 99(5):463-472
primary_sources.role: Discovery of the DR5::GUS distal auxin maximum in the Arabidopsis root quiescent center and columella initials, and demonstration of proximal QC respecification following NPA polar transport inhibition or laser ablation

six_perturbation_regimes.description: Wild-Type (WT): intact rootward stele PIN1 (v_s = 1.6), shootward epidermal PIN2 (v_e = 1.2), and lateral cortex/endodermis reflux (k_lat = 0.18) with shoot influx J_in = 0.25

Shoot Decapitation (J_in = 0 after steady-state loading): tests Grieneisen et al. (2007) Fig. 3 prediction that the root tip reflux loop acts as a self-sustaining capacitor maintaining >85% of the QC auxin maximum without shoot supply
pin2 / eir1 Mutant (v_e = 0.08): loss of shootward epidermal/lateral-root-cap PIN2 efflux traps auxin in the distal tip and shortens the proximal reflux loop and meristematic zone

Lateral Reflux Ablation (k_lat = 0): loss of inward PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 lateral reflux across cortex and endodermis breaks the reverse-fountain loop, letting auxin escape shootward in the epidermis and collapsing the QC capacitor

NPA Polar Transport Inhibition (v_s = 0.05, v_e = 0.05, k_lat = 0.01): global PIN efflux blockade flattens the QC exponential capacitor into a near-uniform diffusive profile (amplification ~ 1.3x) and collapses meristem zonality

QC Laser Ablation & Proximal Regeneration: ablation of distal QC/columella boundary (z <= 60 um) interrupts downward stele discharge and triggers de novo proximal auxin accumulation peak and new QC specification at z ~ 105 um within hours (Grieneisen et al. 2007 Fig. 4; Sabatini et al. 1999)

specimen_metadata.description: Three-panel confocal micrograph (DAPI nuclear blue channel, Alexa Fluor 488 cortical/mitotic microtubule green channel, and merged overlay) of an Arabidopsis thaliana primary root apex showing longitudinal cell files across the stele, cortex, epidermis, quiescent center, and root cap, together with dense mitotic divisions in the high-PLT meristematic zone.
